brief: GS prime brokerage data: US long-onlies and hedge funds closed a hectic week as moderate net sellers, with supply concentrated in tech. Aggregate net TMT (Info Tech + Comm Services) selling over the past two weeks is ~$20bn, approaching the ~$23bn sold over two weeks during July's AI selling episode. Mood remains poor and performance challenges persist. Unlike last week, when AI selling rotated into defensive pockets, this week saw almost no such rotation despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and parts of Financials. US equities were net sold for a third straight week (four of the last five), driven by long-and-short Single Stock sales, the largest de-grossing since late July. Industrials was among the most net sold sectors, with hedge funds selling it at the fastest pace in six-plus months, while Real Estate and Staples were the most net bought, reinforcing a defensive posture. Gross leverage rose to 216.1% (64th percentile, one year) while net leverage fell to 43.4% (0th percentile, five years). Next week brings FOMC, BOC, ECB and BOJ decisions, the heaviest Q3 earnings week (44% of S&P market cap, including MSFT, GOOG, NOW, KLAC, AMZN, INTC), a 1.80% S&P implied move through next Friday, and Brazil's election Sunday, where Polymarket gives Bolsonaro a 76% win chance versus a slimmer local-poll lead.
